title: Every nontrivial finite tree has at least two leaves
statement: Let $G$ be a tree on a finite vertex set $V$ with at least two vertices. Then $G$ has at least two leaves: there exist distinct vertices $u, v \in V$ with $\deg(u) = 1$ and $\deg(v) = 1$.
hypotheses_covered: vertex set is nontrivial (at least two vertices)
replaced:
\emph{Every nontrivial tree has at least two vertices of degree
one.}
